text:
sam: heads-up — CI showed a ~6% MRR jump on the quantized embedding runner for the new model after merge, looks flaky :thinking:
marta: saw that in the dashboard, weird alignment across unrelated PRs :eyes:
kevin: any repro locally? CI link?
sam: https://ci.internal/runs/89321 — logs attached. The runner test set versus baseline changed ordering for ~12 queries.
ci-bot: test run 89321 finished · 1 failed, 2 flaky · artifacts: /artifacts/89321
marta: quick skim — the shuffling in eval_runner.process_batch seems non-deterministic. I think the global numpy RNG was touched by a helper import.
jia: we initialize np.random.seed at process start in one place, but some utils call np.random.shuffle without a local rng
kevin: ah — so parallel workers race on global RNG -> order changes -> deterministic metrics that rely on stable tie-breakers get different MRR/NDCG
sam: exact. baseline runner assumed deterministic ordering of ties (stable sort). With shuffle bleed we break ties differently and rerank NDCG jumps.
leo: proposed patch: replace np.random.shuffle(...) with rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) or better, use deterministic torch.Generator per worker.
marta: +1. Also add a test that runs the harness twice with fixed seeds and asserts identical sort order for identical inputs.
kevin: can we add CI gating to catch seed bleed? maybe a regression test that compares metric deltas > eps -> fail.
jia: I pushed a small PR to use default_rng per worker and added stable_sort in rerank comparator: https://git/internal/pr/421
sam: running local loop 50x now. after patch, MRR variance went from 0.053 to 0.0004 across runs.
ci-bot: scheduled rerun for PR 421 · run 89400
leo: also consider instrumenting the harness to log the first 10 orderings for a query when metric delta > threshold to aid debugging in future.
marta: good idea. add a short JSON blob with seed, worker-id, ordering so we can trace back quickly.
kevin: nice catch. this would have been annoying to root in a production rollout. :relieved:
sam: I'll merge after green CI and follow up with a small dashboard note about deterministic-run expectations.
jia: created ticket ML-1243 to add a broader audit for global RNG usage across the repo.
leo: FYI, this affected quantized and fp16 runners similarly because ordering/tie-breaking is orthogonal to numeric type.
marta: closing loop — once PR passes, let's run the full mteb-like suite and post results to #eng-ml-metrics.
sam: thanks everyone, saved us from a noisy deploy.
